abstract: Amyloid {beta}-protein (A{beta}), which is known for its role in Alzheimer's disease (AD), is also involved in several physiological functions. Of the two predominant isoforms, A{beta}40 and A{beta}42, the latter is more aggregation-prone and more active in health and disease. In the brain, A{beta} interacts with free lipids, which may affect its assembly pathways. Here, thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence spectroscopy is combined with molecular dynamics (MD) to investigate A{beta}40 and A{beta}42 co-assembly with free dimyristoylphosphatidylcholine (DMPC) and DMPC/cholesterol (CHOL) lipids. ThT measurements at several protein-to-lipid (PL) ratios show isoform- and lipid composition-dependent kinetics of A{beta} fibril formation with clear isoform-dependent lipid effects at a PL ratio of 1:5. Early co-assembly stages of six A{beta}40/A{beta}42 with DMPC and DMPC/CHOL lipids at this PL ratio are then examined by MD. MD results indicate that lipids alter the secondary structure more and interact more avidly with A{beta}40 than with A{beta}42. In turn, A{beta}40 increases the planar order of lipid bicelles more than A{beta}42. Unlike A{beta}40, A{beta}42 decreases the nematic order of CHOL. In DMPC/CHOL lipids, A{beta}42 but not A{beta}40 exhibits two A{beta}-lipid interaction modes associated with mutually exclusive A{beta}42-lipid and A{beta}42-A{beta}42 interactions. Our MD findings provide a plausible explanation for an experimentally observed increase in the lag time for A{beta}40 fibril formation in DMPC lipids and even more so in DMPC/CHOL lipids that contrasts with much smaller effects of lipids on A{beta}42 fibril formation and offer additional atomistic-level insights into A{beta} co-assembly with lipids amenable to experimental testing.

summary: ThT kinetics and MD simulations show Aβ40 and Aβ42 co-assemble with DMPC and DMPC/cholesterol lipids differently, explaining isoform-specific lag-time effects.
title: Distinct Aβ40 and Aβ42 co-assembly pathways with free lipids: Experiment-driven MD study
